name: Class G2 Entry Permit (Employed Expatriates)

requirements.blocker_text: Appointment letter from a Ugandan employer plus an agency covering letter.
Employer must show proof of failure to employ a qualified Ugandan for the role, plus submit an employee roster showing nationalities and positions.
Certified graduate-level qualifications relevant to the role.

outcome.duration_length: 6 months (USD 1,250), 12 months (USD 2,500), 24 months (USD 5,000), or 36 months (USD 7,500) -- all beyond 6 months include a USD 1,500 non-refundable component

sources.title: Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control, Uganda -- Class G2 Entry Permit (foreign expatriates employed in Uganda, including salaried NGO employees): fee scale USD 1,250 (6mo) / 2,500 (12mo) / 5,000 (24mo) / 7,500 (36mo); requires appointment letter, police/Interpol clearance, tax clearance, certified graduate qualifications, and proof of failure to employ a qualified Ugandan

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Uganda). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- tier-1 DCIC sourced, directly fetched by me. Explicit, formally-documented labour-market test built directly into the permit's evidence requirements ('proof of failure to employ a qualified Ugandan'), a genuinely clear structural feature not left implicit the way some other countries in this dataset handle it. Class G1 (missionaries/NGO volunteers) and Class G3 (rare-skilled expatriates in agro-processing/manufacturing/mining) share the same G-series structure but were not modeled as separate files -- disclosed here as close variants of this route rather than fragmenting into near-duplicate files. citizenship_after_months (120 = 10yr) cross-referenced from ug_citizenship_by_residence.json, not independently sourced here.
